blogs.title: Beyond the First Wave: Navigating Multiphasic Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: This post explores the clinical challenges of biphasic and multiphasic anaphylaxis—where symptoms recur after an initial resolution. We will discuss the current lack of consensus on monitoring durations, the difficulty of identifying reliable predictors for relapse, and how to differentiate true biphasic reactions from ongoing allergen absorption or refractory anaphylaxis.

blogs.title: Is 0.3mg Enough? Rethinking Epinephrine Dosing in the Obese Patient
blogs.description: A critical look at the dose-response relationship in anaphylaxis management. We analyze the potential dangers of relying on 0.3mg epinephrine auto-injectors for adults over 50kg, discussing evidence that suggests a higher risk of escalation in care when standard 0.5mg doses are bypassed due to availability or clinician hesitancy.

blogs.title: The Steroid Debate: Do Corticosteroids Actually Prevent Biphasic Reactions?
blogs.description: We examine the shifting evidence regarding the role of corticosteroids in anaphylaxis. While still widely used in many hospital protocols to prevent biphasic reactions, recent systematic reviews suggest no evidence of benefit and potential risks of increased admission. This post evaluates where the evidence stands and why clinical practice often lags behind the data.

blogs.title: The Hidden Driver: Systemic Mastocytosis and Anaphylaxis Risk
blogs.description: What happens when a patient presents with unusually complex or refractory anaphylaxis? This post looks at underlying pathologies like systemic mastocytosis. We discuss how mast cell disorders can predispose patients to severe reactions and the importance of early tryptase measurement and screening for systemic clues like hepatomegaly.

blogs.title: Proactive vs. Reactive: Management Tensions in Recurrent Anaphylaxis
blogs.description: When a patient experiences multiple relapses of anaphylactic shock despite standard treatment, how do you proceed? We weigh the clinical tensions between preemptive continuous IV epinephrine versus an expectant management approach, analyzing the risks, benefits, and the lack of clear evidence-based guidelines for multiphasic cases.
